description: Notes from the human editor directing the curmudgeon to review specific items with specific focus areas. Check at the start of every run. Pending notes take priority over the normal tracker sequence. Mark notes as consumed after reviewing.

notes.topic: WIN-010 cycle 18: narrow deep-attack review of EXP-684-rev2 (c17 fixes plus the new BOU 2017 Z evidence), before integration
notes.context: WIN-010.c17 (q609) approved EXP-684 rev1 subject to sentence-level fixes (ISS-3110 Chapman 1933 mis-citation, ISS-3111 batch). The analyst's rev2 (2026-09-29) goes beyond those fixes. To source the amplitude (c17 hole 1), it adds Meza et al. 2022 and its own INTERMAGNET-definitive computation. Together these show BOU Z was NOT depressed at the 2017 eclipse relative to quiet days (+0.8 nT at 17:20, +4.9 nT at maximum), and that the dome's -18.22 nT is matched by ordinary quiet days (-9.3 to -27.3 nT). That is a new evidential argument in a verdict-bearing panel, so it must not integrate unreviewed. This note commissions the cycle directly. No decider queue push is needed.
scope_artifacts: monitor/analyst/analysis-records/win010-c17-rev2-verification-20260929.json - BOU Z check + DE440s, scripts and checksums
notes.mechanism: Single operator-commission review, cycle 18, deep-attack, narrow scope. Takes priority over the normal queue this run. Write reviews/WIN-010.c18.json.
review_focus_hints: (i) Attack the BOU Z computation from BOTH sides. Check the quiet-day selection, the baseline definition, the timing (local vs UT), and INTERMAGNET vs USGS data (USGS returns Z=99999 for Aug 2017). Did we pick a reference that happens to erase the dome's number? Would a reasonable alternative reference reproduce the dome's -10.9 / -18.22 nT as an eclipse effect?

(ii) Check the Meza et al. 2022 reading against the paper itself. Confirm authors, title, DOI and that it says dZ at BOU was small and positive with the signal mainly in dX. We have had three citation failures in this cluster (Kim & Chang 2018, the Hartland 'NASA calculation', Chapman 1933); do not accept a citation on the analyst's paraphrase.

(iii) Answer the verdict question: 'Std Model Explains' vs 'Refuted by Data'. If the dome's specific observed number is a baseline artefact, is 'Std Model Explains' now too generous to the dome, or too harsh to it? Whichever you pick, give the rule so it can be applied symmetrically to our own claims.
(iv) Spot-verify the c17 hole 0-10 fixes, especially hole 0 (Chapman 1933 now described as a theoretical expectation that the observations of the time did not show) and the AACGM latitude numbers.

(v) Public-date text must read 2026-10-31. The post-event paragraph must say plainly that our binary profile failed (per c3 C3-3), OR state that the post-event result waits for EXP-687. It must not read as though the pre-event expectation held.
